text: DSH 网页端的 Hindsight 记忆设置伴随插件，会在设置页提供一个表单，用来查看和编辑 ~/.hindsight/coding-agent.json。页面按连接、记忆库路由、召回、知识页、写入保留、数据导入和范围开关等分组展示配置，也提供按 bank 查看和编辑覆盖值的标签页。它通过主机服务读写配置文件，支持修改字段、清除字段以回退到环境变量或默认值，并保留未知配置项；密钥值会隐藏。适合希望通过 DSH 图形界面管理 Hindsight 配置的用户；需要安装并启用 Hindsight 插件。

DSH web companion for editing Hindsight settings in ~/.hindsight/coding-agent.json. Its page groups connection, routing and retention, with per-bank overrides. The host service preserves unknown keys and lets users clear values to restore defaults. Secret values are hidden; enable Hindsight too.
想在 DSH 设置里直接修改 Hindsight 的配置文件。
如何给不同项目的 Hindsight 记忆库设置不同参数？
I want a settings page to edit the Hindsight options used by my DSH workspace.
DSH Hindsight Settings 的功能「配置页编辑」：在设置页查看并修改 Hindsight 的共享 JSON 配置，也可按 bank 查看和保存覆盖项。保存时只更新变更字段。
使用前须知：apiToken 是敏感字段，页面只显示是否已设置，不返回明文；可输入新值替换或显式清除。（见 src/service.ts:155-159）
@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings 的维护与更新元数据：已弃用；距最后推送 30 天；提交数 9；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 25/100（置信度 low）。

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · @Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings：It is a companion on purpose. `@vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents` mounts as a **subpath row**
(`…/coding-agents/dsh`), and DSH's client module system only attaches a browser half to the row whose
specifier is the bare package name — so that package cannot carry a settings page without changing how
every existing user mounts it. Nor does it declare any `Config`: it imports nothing from dsh and
resolves its settings from its own file, which the shipped settings form (schema-derived, persisted
into the profile patch) cannot reach. This package therefore ships its own page and its own host
service, and leaves the plugin untouched.

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · Any profile except a packaged Desktop one, whose profile the CLI refuses to write:：dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings

In the **desktop app** (the profile the Electron shell owns) the CLI refuses by design; install from

`git push` does not silently change what you run: re-install (or update) to move it. Git installs
build nothing — the compiled `lib/` is committed — so the install is a checkout, not a build.bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add '@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings@github:Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings'

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · The one manual step：A package's bundle is mounted only when the profile selects it in `dsh.profile.bundles`, and dsh's own
plugin-manager README states that "an unselected plain dependency is left out" — the manager lists
bundles a dependency supplies but does NOT select them. So after installing this package, enable
**Hindsight** once in **Settings → Plugins** (installing the bundle by name,
`dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @vectorize-io/hindsight-coding-agents`, does the same thing).

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · The one manual step：`dsh` has no bundle-depends-on-bundle field to express this (`DshManifest` carries only
`manifestVersion`, `bundle.patch`, `client`, `engines.dsh`), and the alternative — our patch inserting
Hindsight's row directly — would compose the same row twice when its own bundle is also enabled,
because patch `insert` appends without deduplicating entry ids.

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · How it works：```
~/.hindsight/coding-agent.json          ← the one file every Hindsight harness reads
        ▲            │
        │ apply()    │ describe()                     (host, src/service.ts + src/typert.host.ts)
        │            ▼

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · How it works：- The host publishes one Cordis service; its `./typert` manifest exposes `describe` and `apply` to the
  page (`docs/api-gateway.md`).
- The page renders every field from `src/fields.ts` — the single declaration of the config surface —
  and writes back only what changed. A field the user clears is sent as `null`, which removes the key
  so the setting falls back to the environment variable, then to the plugin's own default.
- Fields are grouped into one tab per section, plus a **按项目（banks）** tab. A bank tab edits
  `banks.<id>`, which is how upstream lets one repository differ from the shared top level; opening a
  bank calls `describe({ kind: "bank", id })` and saving calls `applyScoped(...)`. `paths.<dir>` is
  listed read-only.
- A field the file does not set is still shown with its **effective** value — the plugin default —
  labelled as such, while a cleared cell still means "remove the key". Nothing is written until a cell
  actually changes.
- Secrets are never sent to the page: `apiToken` shows as set-but-blank ("已设置（不显示明文）"), typing
  replaces it, and only the explicit 清空 button removes it. This mirrors dsh's own set

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · Safety：- Managed keys only: keys this package does not know, and the nested `banks` / `paths` / `harnesses`
  sections, are preserved verbatim.
- `null` removes a key; there is no other way to delete, and a field the page never sends is untouched.
- Writes go through a temp file + rename, at mode `0600` — the file can hold `apiToken`.
- A file that cannot be parsed is **never** overwritten: the page reports it and disables saving.
- An invalid value (wrong type, unknown key, a file-only nested map) is refused before the disk is
  touched.

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · Interface fields：`mapPathToBank`, `pages`, `customPages`, `recallOptions`, `retainMetadata`, `defaultBankConfig`,
`harnesses` and the deprecated `autoReflect` are shown **read-only** in a group tab: they are nested
maps a single form field cannot express, and upstream documents them as file-only. The page says so
per field rather than hiding them. `banks` and `paths` are not read-only: the bank tab edits
`banks.<id>` through a scoped write, and the file's `paths` sections are listed read-only.

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · Precedence and when an edit takes effect：Upstream resolves `defaults → HINDSIGHT_* → the file's top level → harnesses.<name> → banks.<id> /
paths.<dir>`, later winning. The page writes the top level, so a `harnesses.dsh` entry for the same key
still wins — the page badges those fields. Upstream reads the file once per workspace, at plugin load,
so an edit reaches a running session after a dsh restart; `apiToken` is the exception (its client
re-reads the credential on the next call after a server rejection, so rotating it needs no restart).
section: Precedence and when an edit takes effect

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · Development：```bash
npm install --legacy-peer-deps   # pinned in .npmrc: npm's arborist crashes on vitest's peer set
npm test                         # host service, the file rules, the field table's drift guard
npm run build                    # lib/index.js + lib/typert.host.js (host) and lib/client.js (browser)
npm run test:smoke               # bundle shape / laziness / registration smoke test

@Echo-Note/dsh-hindsight-settings README · Development：Both halves land in `lib/`, so `npm run build` removes `lib/` once and then builds host → client; use
`npm run build:host` / `npm run build:client` only when you mean to rebuild one half.

`src/fields.ts` is the single declaration of the config surface. `src/upstream.test.ts` checks it
against the **installed** Hindsight plugin (its bundle keeps the source shape), so upgrading that
plugin fails this package's tests instead of silently hiding a new setting.
